newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Japan cobalt consumption to hit 6,500 tonnes in 97.
newsitem.headline: Japan cobalt consumption to hit 6,500 tonnes in 97.

text.p: Japan's primary cobalt consumption in 1997 will jump to 6,500 tonnes from 5,700 tonnes last year, a Japanese industry official said on Thursday.

"In 1997, we anticipate 6,500 metric tonnes of primary cobalt consumption in Japan at present," Ryoichi Terada, assisant general manager of the cobalt section at Mitsui & Co Ltd, told a conference in Hong Kong.
"We are convinced that 10,000 metric tonnes per year of cobalt consumption is well possible in Japan at the beginning of the 21st century," he said.
He said that critical price fluctuations would accelerate efforts for substitution of cobalt and called for price stability.

"We therefore expect the cobalt industry will encourage cobalt demand by achieving more stability of the supply structure and stability of price at a reasonable level for the benefit of both consumers and suppliers," he said.
Traders at the conference have said the price of cobalt could rise to US$30 per pound.
On Wednesday, cobalt was quoted at $24.25/25.25 per pound for cathodes and $21.75/22.75 per pound for ingots.
Currently, battery applications represent more than one third of total cobalt consumption in Japan, or approximately 2,100 tonnes in 1996, according to Mitsui's estimates.
The second largest primary application is cobalt sulphates for videotape applications, representing consumption of 750 to 800 tonnes of cobalt in 1996, Terada said.
Terada said official statistics did not always reflect reality.

"Otherwise, it is very difficult to explain huge differences between official statistics (by the Trade Ministry) and import statistics of more than 2,000 metric tonnes a year in the past years," Terada said.
In 1996, Zambia and Zaire represented about 50 percent of total Japanese imports despite considerable production decreases in the first half of the 1990s.
"Supply from the two African producers has been fairly stable over the period," Terada said, adding that the figures were 2,300 tonnes in 1992 versus 2,600 tonnes in 1996.
Cobalt oxide imports have increased from 270 tonnes in 1992 to 850 tonnes in 1996, he said.
